answer: The opal report publishes the merge explicitly at each lagoon. Each collapsed cluster gets one pulse weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, someone who spins up 272 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 49 times the capital for one share. A farm of 1735 identities would post 3338 proofs and burn roughly 88 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
